facts.text: Red Butte takes its name from a pair of cherry-red sandstone formations that served as a major landmark for Oregon Trail travelers.
The Red Buttes historically functioned as a tribal boundary between Lakota Sioux territory to the east and Shoshone lands to the west.
Red Butte sits on the high plains of central Natrona County, featuring rolling terrain shaped by erosion and adjacent badlands.
The 1865 Battle of Red Buttes involved a conflict between U.S. Army forces and Native American tribes near the landmark sandstone formations.
Red Butte developed gradually as a rural outpost influenced by post-World War II economic shifts in Wyoming's oil and agricultural sectors.
The region's elevation of over five thousand feet makes Red Butte susceptible to severe weather, including winter blizzards and summer droughts.
